name: Shotcut
summary: A free, open-source video editor for Windows, Mac and Linux.
description: Shotcut is a free, open-source desktop video editor. You can use it to trim and arrange clips on a timeline, add titles, transitions and audio, and export a finished video. Because it is open source there is no paid edition to upgrade to, and it runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. It is a sensible starting point when you want to edit videos on a computer without paying or creating an account.

pricing.free_tier_details: Free and open source; the official site describes it as 'a free, open source, cross-platform video editor'.

key_capabilities.text: Free, open-source, cross-platform video editing for Windows, Mac and Linux.

limitations.text: Desktop only: the official site lists Windows, Mac and Linux, with no web or mobile version.

getting_started: Download Shotcut from the official website for your operating system.
Import a few clips, drag them to the timeline and practise trimming.
Export a short test video to check the settings work on your device.
